tagline.text: The Philippines' only double barrier reef and marine protected area, stretched across the sea north of Bohol

location.label: Location
location.text: Between Bohol's northern coast and the Camotes Sea (off Talibon, Bien Unido and Getafe, continuing toward Cebu and Leyte)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: 1 day (boat trip from Talibon or Bien Unido)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,000–3,000 (per person for a day trip, estimated using public transport and a shared boat; confirm locally)

children.text: Danajon Bank is a double barrier reef of about 272 km² in the Camotes Sea north of Bohol, widely described as the only one in the Philippines. Unlike Panglao it is barely developed and quiet, and you can reach it by boat from Talibon or Bien Unido to snorkel and visit the underwater shrine.

Danajon Bank is a double barrier reef in the Camotes Sea, between Bohol's northern coast and Cebu and Leyte. English Wikipedia describes it as about 156 km long, about 272 km² in area and containing roughly 40 islands, and Guinness World Records lists it at about 271.7 km² as the "largest double barrier reef." Many sources agree there are only six double barrier reefs in the world and that this is the only one in the Philippines. It is said to consist of an outer barrier about
11 km
offshore and an inner reef close to the coast that is up to
2 km
wide, running side by side.

The reef is said to be the result of about 6,000 years of coral growth on a submarine ridge. The outer barrier is called the Caubyan Outer Reef on the Cebu side and the inner one the Calituban Inner Reef on the Bohol side, and three passes (northwest, middle and northeast) cut between the two barriers. It is also presented as a geosite within the Bohol Island UNESCO Global Geopark. So think of it less as a one-photo attraction and more as an entire sea with a story of earth science and marine conservation.

Danajon Bank borders several Bohol municipalities, including Talibon, Bien Unido, Getafe, Buenavista, Calape, Tubigon and Inabanga, as well as Bato in Leyte and Lapu-Lapu City in Cebu. More than 30 marine protected areas (MPAs) have been declared, and in September 2022 the Bohol provincial government signed an agreement with the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) and the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) to create the Bohol Danajon Bank Double Barrier Reef Management Council. The council held its first regular meeting in Talibon in July 2023. Its goals are conservation, food security, local livelihoods and ecotourism, and declaring a protected seascape is also on its agenda.

The best-known spot for visitors is the Bien Unido Double Barrier Reef Marine Park. Wikipedia says it was established in 2012 and is described as the "first underwater pilgrimage in Asia." Inside it, a Santo Niño statue lies at a depth of 6–9 m, which can be seen while snorkeling, and a statue of Our Lady of Danajon lies deeper, at 24–30 m. On the Talibon side, trips are combined with an interpretive center about the reef-protection movement and sea outings such as the Bongan sandbar. Not every site is a polished tourist attraction, though, so always confirm itineraries and boats locally.

blocks.title: The Philippines' only double barrier reef

children.text: The outer and inner barriers run side by side, a form said to exist in only six places in the world. Guinness World Records also lists it as the largest double barrier reef. Just watching the color of the water change from the boat gives you a feel for the landform.

The Santo Niño statue lies at 6–9 m and can be seen while snorkeling, while the Our Lady of Danajon statue lies at 24–30 m, about 2 km away, and is for divers only. It is a marine park, so follow local rules and guidance, and whether you can go on a given day depends on sea conditions.
This sandbar off Talibon is said to be
20–30 minutes
away by boat and is presented as a place for swimming, snorkeling and scuba diving. Its size and condition change a lot with the tide, so check before you set out.

Most of the small islands on Danajon are home to fisherfolk, and some are said to be among the most densely populated islands in the world. From the boat you can see the scenery of fishing island villages.

Parrotfish, wrasses and anemonefish live among the corals, the seagrass beds are nurseries for young fish and the mangroves are spawning habitat, according to sources. Seahorses are also described as a draw, but there is no evidence that you can see them at a set spot, so ask your guide.

Wikipedia notes endangered corals such as mushroom coral, bubble coral and elegance coral. One local news report (September 2023) says dugongs use these waters as habitat, but I could not confirm it in other sources. Neither is guaranteed for ordinary travelers, so treat a sighting as a bonus.

The Bohol Tourism Office's tour description includes a visit to the Talibon Interpretive Center, which retraces the community's efforts to protect the Danajon double barrier reef. The description does not give exhibits, fees or opening hours, so inquire in advance.

In 2023 a Bohol Danajon double barrier reef conservation project was launched in Talibon, and marine conservation groups and local governments are working against dynamite fishing and overfishing. Following the rules as a visitor is itself a contribution to conservation.

items.title: One day from Talibon
items.subtitle: Interpretive center, sandbar and sea trip

children.text: Leave Tagbilaran for Talibon in the north by bus or van. Depending on the route the distance is
, and general guides say it takes close to
3 hours
. Staying overnight in Talibon the day before makes the morning much easier.

At Talibon port, check for a local boat and guide. Mornings often bring lighter wind and calmer seas, so leave as early as you can. Boat prices vary with group size and itinerary, so settle the price before you set out.
Head out by boat toward the Bongan sandbar and snorkel. It is said to be about
20–30 minutes
one way, and you may not be able to go if the sea is rough.
Return to Talibon for lunch. If you have time, check whether the interpretive center is open. The tour description gives no regular exhibit schedule.
Finish with a walk along the coastal road or around the church, and check your onward transport for the same day in advance.
This itinerary means finding a local boat yourself rather than joining a fixed group tour. The Bohol Tourism Office's package is described as a day trip from
in the morning to
in the evening (about 10.5 hours). This comes from a single listing that I could not confirm elsewhere, so use the times only for comparison and check with the office when you book.
Travel from Tagbilaran to Bien Unido, about
108 km
away. Wikipedia says the road trip takes more than 2 hours.

Check the visit procedure and a boat at the Bien Unido marine park office or the tourism office. The underwater shrine is reported to have no mooring buoys, so confirm with the boatman where to drop anchor.
Snorkel near the Santo Niño statue. At a depth of
it is said to be visible from the surface on a clear day. Follow the safety rules and guidance.
Return to land for a meal and, if time allows, look around nearby coastal villages before heading back.
The Our Lady of Danajon statue at 24–30 m can only be reached by people with diving certification. Look into dive shops and schedules separately.
There are direct flights from Manila (NAIA) to Bohol-Panglao International Airport (TAG). The flight takes roughly
1 hour 20 minutes
, so check the airline's latest schedule.
Another way is to fly to Cebu (Mactan, CEB) and take a boat across to Talibon or Tubigon in northern Bohol.
From Panglao airport to Talibon it takes more than
2 hours
by car, so plan your lodging around your arrival time.
A fast craft from Cebu City pier to Talibon is said to take about
2 hours
, and Bien Unido sources also say a fast craft from Cebu to Talibon takes over 2 hours.
Aggregator sites list a fast craft at about ₱500 one way and a RoRo at about ₱350–450, with the RoRo taking about
4 hours
, but operating days and times change often, so check with the operator.
Small boat routes between Getafe and Cebu are also mentioned, but schedules must be confirmed locally.
Buses and vans to Talibon leave from the Tagbilaran Integrated Bus Terminal and are described as taking roughly
2.5 to 3.5 hours
depending on route and stops, and aggregator sites list about ₱140–170 as of 2026. Fuel surcharges may push fares higher, so confirm locally.
Bien Unido lies farther east of Talibon. There is no confirmed timetable for connecting from Talibon by local transport, so ask locally.
Distances within Talibon, Bien Unido and Getafe are short, and many people use motorcycle taxis or tricycles.
Visiting the reef itself requires a boat, and this means a locally hired boat rather than a scheduled route.
Danajon Bank can be visited all year, but seas and visibility vary by season. The underwater shrine listing treats November to June as the best time to visit, with water temperatures of about 27–30℃.
The Camotes Sea has many windy days, so it is best to set out early in the morning. If a tropical depression or monsoon passes, boats may not run, so leave plenty of slack in your schedule.

Most travelers who come to see Danajon Bank stay in Talibon town. It is not a resort area like Panglao's beaches, so lodging is mostly small hotels and guesthouses, and booking ahead is safer in peak season. Prices and operating status change often, so check the latest information.

Meals center on restaurants and the market in Talibon town. Many people say the seafood is fresh in this fishing area, and chicken dishes, rice and local snacks are also easy to find. When heading out to the islands, bring your own drinking water and snacks.
Even for a day trip, leaving from Tagbilaran makes the round trip long, so we recommend spending a night in Talibon or Bien Unido.
Boats are often priced per boat rather than per person, so gather a group and split the cost.
Before you go, contact the local tourism office to confirm the visit procedure, fees and available dates.
Leaving early in the morning often means lighter wind and calmer seas.
Snorkeling gear rental may not be set up locally, so bring your own if you can.
Do not step on or touch the coral, and watch out for sea urchins and jellyfish.
Bring a waterproof bag, a waterproof phone pouch and sunscreen (a reef-friendly product).
Carry plenty of cash in pesos. Small ports may not have ATMs.
This is not a managed attraction but the fishers' sea, so confirm boats, prices and rules locally and give up the trip if the weather is bad.
If the weather is bad, boats may not run or may have to turn back.
Dynamite fishing and overfishing have damaged the coral in some areas, so follow protected-area rules.
The underwater shrine is reported to have no mooring buoys, so confirm the anchoring spot with your boatman.
Collecting coral, shells and marine life is prohibited, and do not touch protected species such as dugongs.
Always wear a life jacket, and if you are not confident in the water, snorkel only in shallow areas.

Getafe is a coastal town on Bohol's northwest side, and Pandanon is a small island between Mactan in Cebu and Bohol. Confirm schedules locally.
